anne: Quick sync - FinServX asks for PrivateDeploy but their SecOps requires original client IPs in logs AND a deny-by-default egress policy. They prefer minimal network changes. Can we list feasible options + a short pasteable firewall block? POC target next week.

kevin: Options brief: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) = minimal approval friction but endpoint ENI will be source IP (so network-layer src IP lost). VPC Peering or TGW preserves src IP but needs routing/peering approvals. NLB + Proxy Protocol can preserve app-level IPs without peering if we can run an NLB that speaks proxy protocol.

lia: For the egress allowlist: prefer FQDNs on their corporate proxy. If they demand CIDRs we provide a small set and request a weekly maintenance window for any rotations. Pasteable snippet below.

kevin: Pasteable firewall snippet (recommend):
```
# Corporate proxy/firewall outbound rules to Redwood PrivateDeploy
ALLOW tcp 443 to private.redwood-inference.net   # API/control plane
ALLOW tcp 443 to downloads.redwood-inference.net # model pulls (schedule during window)
ALLOW tcp 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.net # optional metrics
# CIDR fallback (if proxy cannot FQDN): ALLOW tcp 443 to 198.51.100.0/22
```

lia: Security questionnaire text (pasteable):
"PrivateLink endpoints will present the endpoint ENI IP at the network layer. To retain client identity we support X-Forwarded-For headers with signature validation and Proxy Protocol v2 via an NLB. For customers requiring network-layer source IP preservation, we recommend VPC Peering or Transit Gateway topology. We will provide signed headers and audit logs as part of the PrivateDeploy runbook"

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: sandbox-finservx created in us-west-2. creds in secret manager; docs in drive.

anne: Great — kevin can you draft a 1p decision table + rough 5TB/mo cost bullets? lia, please add TLS-inspect caveat. Send to customer tomorrow.

kevin: On it; rough non-binding: PrivateLink ~$0.02-0.06/GB+endpoint-hour; Peering/TGW lower per-GB but higher ops.

lia: I'll include note: if FinServX TLS-inspects egress, they should exempt our FQDN so SNI reaches endpoint or else PrivateLink routing may fail.

anne: Thanks team.
